questions: Should the function modify the input DataFrame in-place (as the reference solution does by subtracting the mean) or should it work on a copy to avoid side effects?
What should happen if the column contains NaN or infinite values? Should they be dropped, filled, or left as is?
Is the alpha parameter guaranteed to be within a valid range (e.g., 0 < alpha < 1), and if not, should it be validated?
Should the function raise an error if the column has fewer than 3 or more than 5000 observations (Shapiro-Wilk limits), or handle it gracefully?
Does the artificial step using np.mean require that the mean be computed on the original data before any transformation, or after handling missing values?
Should the function return False if the Shapiro-Wilk test raises a warning (e.g., due to ties in data), or only based on the p-value comparison?
Is the column expected to be numeric (int/float), and if it contains non-numeric data, should it raise an error or attempt conversion?
Should the function handle the case where the column exists but is empty (zero rows) by raising an error or returning a specific boolean?
